# TracetoForge

> Browser-based tool that converts photos of physical tools into 3D-printable
> tray inserts and Gridfinity bins. No CAD experience required. Operated by
> Qwikymart LLC, Northeast Ohio. Free tracing and previewing; export credits
> from $9.99 for 20 credits.

## Core
- [Editor](https://tracetoforge.com/editor/): The browser-based photo-to-insert tool. Upload a photo of a tool on paper, auto-trace, export STL/3MF/SVG/DXF.
- [Community Library](https://tracetoforge.com/community/): User-published traces you can drop into your own drawer trays, Gridfinity bins, or Packout inserts. Free to browse and use.
- [Guide](https://tracetoforge.com/guide/): Getting-started workflow, photo tips, and troubleshooting.

## Reference
- [About](https://tracetoforge.com/about/): Company background, founder, what TracetoForge does and doesn't do.
- [Contact](https://tracetoforge.com/contact/): support@tracetoforge.com — bug reports, feature requests, refund inquiries.
- [Privacy](https://tracetoforge.com/privacy/): All photo processing runs in-browser; no images upload to any server.
- [Terms](https://tracetoforge.com/terms/): Terms of service.

## Key facts
- Output formats: STL, 3MF (multi-material), SVG (laser cut), DXF (CNC).
- Recommended filament: PETG for tool inserts (heat-resistant to 80°C).
- Compatible storage systems: Milwaukee Packout, Gridfinity (42mm grid), DeWalt ToughSystem, DeWalt TSTAK, Klein ModBox, Festool Systainer, Bosch L-Boxx, and custom-dimension trays.
- All photo processing runs in-browser; no images upload to any server.
- Pricing: 3 free credits on signup. 20 credits for $9.99. 100 credits for $34.99 (best value). One credit per export.
- Founder: Chris Winland. Operated by Qwikymart LLC.
- Etsy storefront: https://www.etsy.com/shop/TracetoForge
